about: Old Home Distillers is a family farm distillery on historic Campbell Road in Lebanon, Madison County, southeast of Syracuse. Jerry and Marlene Carvell founded it in 2015 in a hundred-year-old stable they converted into a stillhouse, and their sons Aaron and Adam help run it. Everything is made on the farm from New York-grown ingredients, from the corn whiskey that started the business to the bourbons, ryes and gins that followed.

The Barrel-Rested Gin starts as Old Home’s original gin, which is triple-distilled from local corn in copper pot stills and made in a New World style, with juniper sharing the stage with other botanicals rather than dominating. That gin is then rested in one of the distillery’s own used rye whiskey barrels. The wood softens the juniper and brings forward the anise. It is bottled at 90 proof. Old Home suggests it in a Boulevardier, with ginger, or simply on the rocks, places where a gin with a little oak and spice can stand in for whiskey.
